findings.title: Verification walkthrough cannot isolate the two interventions; no early-exit toggle is specified
findings.description:
Step 3 prescribes four ablation runs: baseline (counter-gating, S=1), early-exit only, subdivision only, and both. But the design changes `get_neighbors_first_k`'s counter-gating to an unconditional `break` (Intervention 1) and defines no mechanism to disable early exit. All four commands are identical except `--subdivision-factor`, so:

- Runs 1 and 2 are the same command, as are runs 3 and 4 — the matrix collapses to two configurations.
- The "baseline (S=1, counter-gating — should reproduce slice 145 ~38 TPS)" run is unreachable after the change lands, because counter-gating no longer exists in the kernel.

The parent plan entry and the 148 re-diagnosis note both frame the interventions as complementary and worth comparing, and the design itself discusses their interaction — so the ablation is part of what this slice should demonstrate. The design needs either (a) a config/CLI toggle that restores counter-gating for ablation runs, or (b) an explicit statement that the baseline numbers are carried over from the slice 145/148 measurement records rather than re-run, with the walkthrough reduced to the configurations that are actually reachable. As written, an implementer following the walkthrough cannot produce the comparison the design claims to make.

findings.title: Candidate-count arithmetic contradicts the cited slice 148 re-diagnosis note
findings.description:
The "Interaction with Intervention 1" paragraph states: "With early exit alone at S=1: agents still load 45,000 candidates but exit after ~32. With S=3 alone: candidates loaded drops to ~5000. With both: candidates loaded ~555." The source this rests on (148-notes.rediagnosis.md) gives different numbers:

- S=3 alone: per-cell occupancy drops to ~555, but the 7×7 scan covers 49 cells × 555 ≈ **27,000** candidates, not ~5,000. The note states this explicitly.
- With both interventions: early exit truncates candidates scanned to roughly the first ~32–50 qualifying candidates (the note estimates "~50"), not ~555 — 555 is the per-cell occupancy, not the scanned count.
- "Early exit alone … agents still load 45,000 candidates but exit after ~32" is internally contradictory; with the break, candidates scanned drops to ~50.

The success criteria are empirical gates so this doesn't invalidate them, but the paragraph is the design's central justification for why the two interventions compose, and it materially overstates subdivision's incremental value once early exit is in place (with early exit, subdivision mostly improves the acceptance rate by trimming out-of-radius corner candidates, rather than cutting 45,000 → 555). Correct the figures to match the re-diagnosis note so expectations going into the CUDA gate runs are calibrated.

findings.title: Plan-assigned 7-neighbor benchmark operating point is absent from the design
findings.description: The plan 140 entry for slice 149 states: "the 7-neighbor operating point is a benchmark target," and the 148 re-diagnosis note reinforces it: "At `max_neighbors=7` the counter-gating waste is even more severe … The early-exit gain scales with `candidates_scanned / max_neighbors`, so lower `max_neighbors` → higher gain. The 7-neighbor target is a meaningful operating point to benchmark at." The slice design benchmarks only `max_neighbors=32` (Success Criteria default config, Verification Walkthrough steps 3 and 5) and never mentions the 7-neighbor point. The requirement this leaves unmet: a measurement confirming the early-exit gain at the biologically realistic operating point the plan names for this slice. This is cheap to add — one additional bench run with `max_neighbors=7` in step 3 — or, if it is being deliberately deferred, say so explicitly.

findings.title: A5's primary verification tool is known to be unavailable on the CUDA host
findings.description: A5 cites "confirmed via `nvcc --ptxas-info` or benchmark log." The slice 148 envelope-measurement note (148-notes.envelope-measurement.md, §2A) records that `ptxas`, `cuobjdump`, and `nvcc` are **not installed** on the CUDA host — slice 148 obtained the zero-local-memory confirmation by inspecting the Quadrants PTX cache directly. The "or benchmark log" alternative and Step 4's log-based approach cover this, but A5 should lead with the demonstrated mechanism (PTX cache inspection / bench log) rather than a tool known to be absent on the gate host.

findings.title: Architecture alignment is otherwise sound
findings.description: Positive confirmations: (1) Profile-first principle honored — the slice is grounded in slice 148 Phase 2 measurements and the R5 re-diagnosis rather than assumed bottlenecks. (2) The Tier 2 NFR (60 TPS at N=50k on CUDA) is restated in the Success Criteria section with the slice's own ≥100 TPS headroom gate. (3) Boundaries respected: no changes to `TickResult`, world-server wiring, numpy/numba backends, or the `quadrants-fused` external API — slice 146's consumption contract is preserved and the dependency direction (149 → 145, 146 consumes unchanged API) matches the plan. (4) The A7 seam is deliberately preserved (Option A), matching slice 145's documented swap point. (5) Config validation fails explicitly at config-load time (`ValueError`, no silent clamp), consistent with project conventions, and the S≤8 bound is justified. (6) Scope is proportional: two interventions plus validation, with distance-ranked k-nearest and GPU prefix sum correctly deferred to Out of Scope per the plan.
